I was sitting at home today when I heard the screech and crash of cars colliding, there was no horn blown prior to the crash though, which made me think perhaps it wasn’t a car collision. I slowly walked out my front gate and saw my elderly neighbour COVERED in blood and two pretty fucked up cars.

He had a decent laceration on his forearm and was violently shaking (in shock). I just reacted and shot off into gear, helping him. We didn’t bother calling an ambulance (which wasn’t necessary) just took him to the local GP 2min down the road to get stitched up.

So apparently what happened was this.

While leaving his house he reversed his car up to his front gate and got out to open the gate. He hadn’t put his hand break on and the car was rolling towards the road. In a panic he threw his foot in the car too hit the break and hit the accelerator instead…the car shot off in reverse dragging him with it 7-10m across the road into another parked car and a tree.

Praise God the whole episode wasn’t more serious. I live between two main roads in a busy area. There is ALWAYS people and cars driving/walking by and at this instant there was no one on that road for 5min other than my neighbour and I, could’ve been a WHOLE lot worse.

I’m typing this story out for a few reasons, one is to organise my thoughts about the event and the other is go over some potential lessons.

One lesson was, that in the time of emergency my thoughts didn’t immediately go to Jesus Christ, only after I took care of the problem did He come to mind and I prayed, which I think is a problem and not sure how to work on.

I realised (and I’m not sure how to word my thoughts on this) the importance of maturity? When my neighbour was in crisis, violently shaking and not knowing what to do, I had to take control of the situation. Perhaps in maturity we can help more/efficiently, in turn setting a good example.

Was a rough day and still not sure how to explain my thoughts…

Either way praise God it wasn’t more serious and please pray for my neighbour.

God Bless
